items.title: CALL MEETING TO ORDER.
CALL ROLL.
PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE.

CONSENT AGENDA. (All agenda items listed with the designation of are considered to be routine items by the governing body and will be enacted by one motion. There will be no separate discussion on these items unless a member of the governing body so requests and support by two other members is received. Any item removed from the Consent Agenda will be considered in its normal sequence on the agenda.)
MINUTES FROM REGULAR MEETING OF THE GOVERNING BODY ON DECEMBER 8, 2025.
MINUTES FROM SPECIAL MEETING OF THE GOVERNING BODY ON DECEMBER 10, 2025.
PUBLIC HEARINGS:

Public Hearing for amendments to the City’s 2025-2027 Consolidated Plan and 2025 Program Year Annual Action Plan for the Housing & Community Development Division’s Community Development Block Grant Program.

ORDINANCE –2nd READING – Defining the terms and conditions of employment for sworn officers of the Cheyenne Police Department for January 2026 until the end of the Fiscal Year 2026. (FINANCE COMMITTEE)
items.normKey: defining the terms and conditions of employment for sworn officers of the cheyenne police department for january 2026 until the end of the fiscal year 2026

items.title: ORDINANCE –1st READING – Creating Chapter 1.28, Administrative Inspection Warrants, establishing authority for their issuance, and amending the Municipal Code of the City of Cheyenne, Wyoming, to authorize certain city officials, as specified, to apply for administrative inspection warrants. (SPONSORS – DR. RINNE, MR. SEGRAVE AND MR. WHITE)
items.normKey: creating chapter 1 28 administrative inspection warrants establishing authority for their issuance and amending the municipal code of the city of cheyenne wyoming to authorize certain city officials as specified to apply for administrative

items.title: RESOLUTION – Repealing Resolution No. 6479 and directing the relisting of the Cheyenne Auxiliary Pumping Station located at 1504 Dillon Avenue, Cheyenne, Wyoming for sale or lease, with revised terms to facilitate redevelopment and community benefit. (FINANCE COMMITTEE) (POSTPONED FROM DECEMBER 8, 2025)
RESOLUTION – Designating specified local banks as depositories for municipal funds. (FINANCE COMMITTEE)

RESOLUTION – Authorizing the Mayor and the City Clerk to sign a Final Plat for Airport View, City of Cheyenne, Laramie County, Wyoming (located east of Townsend Place and north of and adjacent to Dell Range Boulevard). (PUBLIC SERVICES COMMITTEE)

RESOLUTION – Authorizing the Mayor and the City Clerk to sign a Final Plat for Scenic Development, 7th Filing, City of Cheyenne, Laramie County, Wyoming (located south of Storey Boulevard, west of Converse Avenue, and north of East Carlson Street). (PUBLIC SERVICES COMMITTEE)

RESOLUTION – Certifying compliance with Wyoming Statute § 15-1-402 for the City-initiated annexation of various tracts of land completely surrounded by current city limits situate in North Cheyenne, generally located south of Storey Boulevard, east of Powderhouse Road, north of Dell Range Boulevard, and west of Ridge Road. (PUBLIC SERVICES COMMITTEE)

RESOLUTION – Authorizing the Mayor and the City Clerk to sign a Final Plat for Golden Meadows 2nd Filing, City of Cheyenne, Laramie County, Wyoming (located west of Connie Drive, north of Dell Range Boulevard, and east of Golden Meadows Lane). (PUBLIC SERVICES COMMITTEE)

RESOLUTION – Approving a sponsorship by Bison Beverage for Cheyenne Frontier Days events occurring July 17 through July 26, 2026, July 23 through August 1, 2027, and July 21 through July 30 2028. (SPONSOR – MR. ESQUIBEL)

RESOLUTION – Adopting the amended 2025-2027 City of Cheyenne Comprehensive Consolidated Plan and the amended 2025 Annual Action Plan, as prepared by the Cheyenne Housing and Community Development Office, and setting the public comment period and public hearings for the plans. (SPONSOR – MR. ESQUIBEL)
LEASES/CONTRACTS/LEGAL:

Memorandum of Understanding between the City of Cheyenne and certain landowners regarding annexation of property south of Storey Boulevard, west of Converse Avenue, north of Dell Range Boulevard and east of Powderhouse Road. (PUBLIC SERVICES COMMITTEE)

Memorandum of Understanding by and between Laramie County, the City of Cheyenne, the Cheyenne Board of Public Utilities, and the Cheyenne/Laramie County Board of Health regarding the management of the ESRI Enterprise Agreement. (Various City Funds) (FINANCE COMMITTEE)
items.action: Approve in an amount not to exceed $36,185.00

items.title: Agreement between the City of Cheyenne and RingCentral, LLC for providing cloud based enterprise telecom services for all City departments and divisions. (General Fund)
CONSIDERATION OF BIDS/PURCHASES/REQUESTS FOR PROPOSALS:

Consideration to Purchase between the City of Cheyenne and Motorola Solutions for ten (10) Motorola Mobile Radios for the Cheyenne Police Department. (2023-2026 Optional 1% Sales Tax Fund) (FINANCE COMMITTEE)
items.action: Approve in an amount not to exceed $82,615.90

items.title: Consideration to Purchase between the City of Cheyenne and Axon Enterprise, Inc. for ten (10) In-Car Camera Systems for the Cheyenne Police Department. (2023-2026 Optional 1% Sales Tax Fund) (FINANCE COMMITTEE)
items.action: Approve in an amount not to exceed $96,974.60

items.title: Consideration of Bid #S-7-26 for an Agreement between the City of Cheyenne and Pole Mountain Electric, Inc., for the Cheyenne Dunbar Field Light Installation project. (2021 Specific Purpose Option Tax Fund, Development Impact Fees and Rec Mill Grant)
APPLICATIONS/LICENSES/PERMITS:

Transfer of ownership of retail liquor license application filed with the City Clerk’s Office for Cheyenne GS, LLC d/b/a Hi Market Cheyenne, 215 E. Lincolnway, Cheyenne, WY (license currently held by Scooters Scoreboard, LLC d/b/a Scooters Scoreboard Bar). (FINANCE COMMITTEE)
ANNOUNCEMENTS/REPORTS/MOTIONS:

Reappointments of Patrick Vann and Patrick Bustos to the Historic Preservation Board; Amy Hernandez and Robert Mathia to the Planning Commission; Nick Pickering, Ray Fertig Jr., and Julie Goode to the Building Code Board of Appeals; Jeffie Wiggins-McMullen to the Fire Civil Service Commission; Carla Winkler to the Police Civil Service Commission; Patti Riesland, Julie Tucker and Michelle Woerner to the Mayor’s Council for People with Disabilities; William Beaman to the City/County Joint Powers Board for Frontier Park Improvements; and Brian Casey, Ryan Gertsch and Travis Shaffer to the Contractor Licensing Board.

Appointments of Jeff White to the Downtown Development Authority Board; Brittany Wardle to the City/County Board of Health; Charity Campfield to the Board of Adjustment; Joseph Ramos to the Housing and Community Development Board; and John Burdick to the Historic Preservation Board.
VOUCHER REPORT.
REVENUE REPORT.

Announcement of a Public Hearing to be held January 12, 2026 at 6:00 p.m. in City Council Chambers, 2101 O’Neil Avenue, Cheyenne, WY, and via electronic conference meeting, to determine whether compliance of annexation conditions required by Wyoming Statute § 15-1-402 exist for the City-initiated annexation of 26 parcels of land totaling roughly 279.98 acres comprised of various tracts of land situate in north Cheyenne generally located south of Storey Boulevard, east of Powderhouse Road, north of Dell Range Boulevard, and west of Ridge Road.

Announcement of a Public Hearing to be held January 12, 2026 at 6:00 p.m. in City Council Chambers, 2101 O’Neil Avenue, Cheyenne, WY, and via electronic conference meeting, for a transfer of ownership of retail liquor license application filed with the City Clerk’s Office for Ace’s Range LLC d/b/a Ace’s Range, 1505 Pioneer Ave., Cheyenne, WY (license currently held by F & G Corporation d/b/a The Green Door).
OTHER BUSINESS:
ADJOURN.

docs.bodySnippet: RECORD OF PROCEEDINGS FOR THE GOVERNING BODY OF THE CITY OF CHEYENNE Office of City Clerk December 22, 2025 The Governing Body of the City of Cheyenne met in regular session on this date beginning at 6:00 p.m. in City Council Chambers and via electronic conference meeting. Present were: MAYOR – Patrick Collins, COUNCIL MEMBERS – Dr. Michelle Aldrich (via Zoom), Dr. Kathy Emmons, Ken Esquibel, Pete Laybourn, Mark Moody, Tom Segrave , Jeff White and Lawrence Wolfe. Absent: Dr. Mark Rinne. Also present: Kylie Soden, City Clerk. The pledge of allegiance was recited. Consent Agenda. (All agenda items listed with the designation of [CA] are considered to be routine items by the governing body and will be enacted by one motion. There will be no separate discussion on these items unless a member of the governing body so requests and support by two other members is received. Any item removed from the Consent Agenda will be considered in its normal sequence on the agenda . Mayor Collins declared a conflict of interest related to agenda item #11 and abstained from voting on the Consent Agenda. Upon request by Mr. Laybourn, and pursuant to support received by Mr. Moody and Mr. Segrave, item #18(b) was removed from the Consent Agenda. Mr. Segrave moved to approve the remaining items , seconded by Mr. White. Motion carried. Voting “yes” – all members of the governing body present with the exception of Mayor Collins who did not vote. [CA] Minutes from Regular Meeting of the Governing Body on December 8, 2025. Motion (per Consent Agenda) carried. [CA] Minutes from Special Meeting of the Governing Body on December 10, 2025. Motion (per Consent Agenda) carried. Mayor Collins opened a public hearing for amendments to the City’s 2025- 2027 Consolidated Plan and 2025 Program Year Annual Action Plan for the Housing & Community Development Division’s Community Development Block Grant Program. Public comment was made by: Wendy Soto, Housing & Community Development Advisory Council. Comments were made by the following members of the governing body: Mayor Collins , Dr. Emmons and Mr. Esquibel. There being no further comments or input and the purpose of the public hearing having been met, Mayor Collins closed the public hearing. ORDINANCE –2nd READING – Defining the terms and conditions of employment for sworn officers of the Cheyenne Police Department for January 2026 until the end of the Fiscal Year 2026. Reporting for Finance Committee, Mr. Laybourn moved to approve on second reading, seconded by Mr. Moody. Motion carried. Voting “yes” – all members of the governing body present. Announcement of a Public Hearing to be held December 22, 2025 at 6:00 p.m. in City Council Chambers, 2101 O’Neil Avenue, Cheyenne, WY, and via electronic conference meeting for amendments to the City’s 2025-2027 Consolidated Plan and 2025 Program Year Annual Action Plan for the Housing & Community Development Division’s Community Development Block Grant Program.

Announcement that a Calcutta benefitting Make-A-Wish Wyoming will be held January 30 - January 31, 2026 at Red Lion Hotel and Conference Center, 204 W. Fox Farm Rd., Cheyenne, WY (10% of proceeds go to the charity).

ORDINANCE –2nd READING – Annexing to the City of Cheyenne, Wyoming, various tracts of land completely surrounded by current City limits situate in eastern Cheyenne, generally located south of Laramie Street, east of T -Bird Drive, north of East Lincolnway and US 30, and west of Parsons Place. Mr. Segrave moved to approve on second reading, seconded by Dr. Emmons. Motion carried. Voting “yes” – all members of the governing body

Finance Committee meeting uh will everyone please uh steal their cell phones or turn off their devices um when making public comment clearly identify yourself to make public comment online use the raise hand function uh in person approach the podium and please turn on the microphone which will turn green when it's on uh no additional business will be discussed following the completion of this agenda so clerk could we have the first item please number 14 ordinance second reading amending section 5.76.050 residential door-to-door solicitor restriction prohibited practices of the municipal code of the city of Cheyenne Wyoming to expand the types of soliciting prohibited at a residence with a posted no solicitors notice to amend the permissible hours of soliciting and to clarify existing code staff report Mr chairman David Hopinson deputy city attorney um and I just wanted to kind of over give an overview of the uh proposed changes in this ordinance frankly the majority of what you see here there is kind of a lot of blue and a lot of red but the majority of what's there is really more clarification as opposed to substantive changes uh to highlight the more substantive changes uh I would go first to subsection B and I point out the language there at the end of that paragraph that says for purposes of this subsection engaging in conduct conducting activities as a door-to-d dooror solicitor shall include persons and then there's five new um sub paragraphs there that frankly are some of which are just more clarifying that this subsection specifically subsection B applies to those entities uh and then there are two additional ones that are are new with this ordinance and essentially what that does is it would apply the or require that those groups listed have to abide by a no solicitation sign on someone's door um and so any of those entities uh and I would highlight particularly uh you see political entities uh religious entities charitable entities that if there a person has a no soliciting sign uh that they would need to abide by that and not um effect essentially not knock on the door disturb the person without a prior invitation so that's the first change that this ordinance makes and then the next one I would highlight is in subsection E uh on page two which changes the timing uh current ordinance uh prohibits solicitation prior to 10 a.m or after 7 p.m and that would be changed to before 7 a.m uh or after sunset and so those are really the two primary changes that this uh ordinance makes the rest are more clean up and and kind of clarifying and docs.bodySnippet: RECORD OF PROCEEDINGS FOR THE GOVERNING BODY OF THE CITY OF CHEYENNE Office of City Clerk November 10, 2025 The Governing Body of the City of Cheyenne met in regular session on this date beginning at 6:00 p.m. at the Laramie County School District #1 Board room and via electronic conference meeting. Present were: MAYOR – Patrick Collins , COUNCIL MEMBERS – Dr. Michelle Aldrich, Dr. Kathy Emmons, Ken Esquibel, Pete Laybourn, Mark Moody, Dr. Mark Rinne , Tom Segrave and Jeff White. Also present: Kylie Soden , City Clerk. The pledge of allegiance was recited. Consent Agenda. (All agenda items listed with the designation of [CA] are considered to be routine items by the governing body and will be enacted by one motion. There will be no separate discussion on these items unless a member of the governing body so requests and support by two other members is received. Any item removed from the Consent Agenda will be considered in its normal sequence on the agenda. Mr. Esquibel moved to approve, seconded by Mr. White. Motion carried. Voting “yes” – all members of the governing body. [CA] Minutes from Regular Meeting of the Governing Body on October 27, 2025. Motion (per Consent Agenda) carried. Mayor Collins opened a public hearing to determine whether compliance of annexation conditions required by Wyoming Statute §15- 1-402 exist for the City- initiated annexation of 20 parcels of land totaling roughly 13.64 acres comprised of various tracts of land and rights-of-way situate in east Cheyenne generally located south of Laramie Street, east of T -Bird Drive, north of East Lincolnway and US 30, and west of Parsons Place. Comment was made by the following member of the governing body: Mayor Collins. P ublic comment was made by: Rex Helm. There being no further comments or input and the purpose of the public hearing having been met, Mayor Collins closed the public hearing. Mayor Collins opened a public hearing to determine whether compliance of annexation conditions required by Wyoming Statute §15-1-402 exist for the Owner-initiated annexation of 3 parcels of land totaling roughly 20.41 acres located northwest of the intersection of Converse Ave and East Carlson St. Comments were made by the following members of the governing body: Dr. Aldrich and Mayor Collins. There being no further comments or input and the purpose of the public hearing having been met, Mayor Collins closed the public hearing. ORDINANCE –3rd READING – Amending Sections 1.4.3, 1.4.4, 5.1.4, 5.7.10 and 5.8.2 of the Unified Development Code to define recreational vehicle parks and campgrounds, designate zone districts for their operation, create specific use standards for recreational vehicle parks campgrounds, and revise manufactured home and parks regulations as necessary. Reporting for Public Services Committee, Mr. Segrave moved to approve on third and final reading, seconded by Dr. Emmons. Mr. Segrave moved to amend by substitute dated October 30, 2025, seconded by Mr. White. Mr. Segrave moved to amend the substitute by removing on page 2 of Attachment A, Community Business Zone ( CB) as an approved zone for campgrounds and recreational parks, seconded by Dr. Aldrich. docs.bodySnippet: RECORD OF PROCEEDINGS FOR THE GOVERNING BODY OF THE CITY OF CHEYENNE Office of City Clerk October 27, 2025 The Governing Body of the City of Cheyenne met in regular session on this date beginning at 6:00 p.m. at the Laramie County School District #1 Board room and via electronic conference meeting. Present were: MAYOR – Patrick Collins , COUNCIL MEMBERS – Dr. Michelle Aldrich, Dr. Kathy Emmons, Ken Esquibel, Pete Laybourn, Mark Moody, Dr. Mark Rinne , Tom Segrave and Jeff White. Also present: Kylie Soden , City Clerk. The pledge of allegiance was recited. Consent Agenda. (All agenda items listed with the designation of [CA] are considered to be routine items by the governing body and will be enacted by one motion. There will be no separate discussion on these items unless a member of the governing body so requests and support by two other members is received. Any item removed from the Consent Agenda will be considered in its normal sequence on the agenda. Upon request by Dr. Aldrich, and pursuant to support received by Mr. White and Mr. Moody, item #11 was removed from the Consent Agenda. Upon request by Mr. Laybourn, and pursuant to support received by Dr. Aldrich and Mr. Moody, items #14(a) and #15(a) were removed from the Consent Agenda. Mr. Segrave moved to approve the remaining items, seconded by Mr. White. Motion carried. Voting “yes” – all members of the governing body. [CA] Minutes from Regular Meeting of the Governing Body on October 13, 2025. Motion (per Consent Agenda) carried. Mayor Collins opened a public hearing for a bar & grill liquor license application filed with the City Clerk's Office for Redbones, LLC d/b/a HamBones Pizza, 415 W. 17th St. Ste. 170 & 180. Public comment was made by: Jason Hammer, HamBones Pizza. Comment was made by the following member of the governing body: Dr. Rinne. There being no further comments or input and the purpose of the public hearing having been met, Mayor Collins closed the public hearing and referred the application to Finance Committee. ORDINANCE –3rd READING – Amending Section 2.2.8, Assigned Zoning, of the Cheyenne Unified Development Code to conform with the comprehensive revision of Laramie County Zoning Regulations. Reporting for Public Services Committee, Mr. Segrave moved to approve on third and final reading, seconded by Mr. White. Motion carried. Voting “yes” – all members of the governing body. (#4646) ORDINANCE –3rd READING – Amending Section 8.60.050, Weeds as a Nuisance, of the Municipal Code of the City of Cheyenne, Wyoming, to revise and clarify provisions and specify conditions under which vegetation does not constitute a nuisance. Mr. Segrave moved to approve on third and final reading, seconded by Dr. Emmons. Motion carried. Voting “yes” – all members of the governing body. (#4647) ORDINANCE –3rd READING – Amending the Official Zoning Map of the City of Cheyenne, changing the zoning classification from P - Public and MUB Mixed- Use Business Emphasis to CBD Central Business District for land located between O’Neil Avenue and Carey Avenue, north of West 19th Street and south of West 22nd Street. Mr. Segrave moved to approve on third and final reading, seconded by Mr. White.

RECORD OF PROCEEDINGS FOR THE GOVERNING BODY OF THE CITY OF CHEYENNE Office of City Clerk October 13, 2025 The Governing Body of the City of Cheyenne met in regular session on this date beginning at 6:00 p.m. at the Laramie County School District #1 Board room and via electronic conference meeting. Present were: MAYOR – Patrick Collins , COUNCIL MEMBERS – Dr. Michelle Aldrich, Dr. Kathy Emmons, Ken Esquibel, Pete Laybourn, Mark Moody, Tom Segrave and Jeff White. Absent: Dr. Mark Rinne . Also present: Luisa McGill, Deputy City Clerk. The pledge of allegiance was recited. A moment of silence was held in honor of Mr. Roybal. Mayor Collins provided a brief tribute to his life of service. Consent Agenda. (All agenda items listed with the designation of [CA] are considered to be routine items by the governing body and will be enacted by one motion. There will be no separate discussion on these items unless a member of the governing body so requests and support by two other members is received. Any item removed from the Consent Agenda will be considered in its normal sequence on the agenda. docs.bodySnippet: RECORD OF PROCEEDINGS FOR THE GOVERNING BODY OF THE CITY OF CHEYENNE Office of City Clerk September 22, 2025 The Governing Body of the City of Cheyenne met in regular session on this date beginning at 6:00 p.m. in Council Chambers and via electronic conference meeting. Present were: MAYOR – Patrick Collins , COUNCIL MEMBERS – Dr. Michelle Aldrich, Dr. Kathy Emmons, Ken Esquibel, Pete Laybourn, Mark Moody, Dr. Mark Rinne , Scott Roybal , Tom Segrave and Jeff White. Also present: Kylie Soden, City Clerk. The pledge of allegiance was recited. Consent Agenda. (All agenda items listed with the designation of [CA] are considered to be routine items by the governing body and will be enacted by one motion. There will be no separate discussion on these items unless a member of the governing body so requests and support by two other members is received. Any item removed from the Consent Agenda will be considered in its normal sequence on the agenda. Dr. Aldrich moved to approve, seconded by Mr. Segrave. Motion carried. Voting “yes” – all members of the governing body. [CA] Minutes from Regular Meeting of the Governing Body on September 8, 2025. Motion (per Consent Agenda) carried. Mayor Collins opened a public hearing for a transfer of ownership of retail liquor license application filed with the City Clerk's Office for Apple Colorado, LLC, d/b/a Applebee's Neighborhood Grill & Bar, 1401 Dell Range Blvd., Cheyenne, WY (license currently held by AB Cheyenne, WY, LLC d/b/a Applebee's Neighborhood Grill & Bar). Public comment was made by: Brain Call, A rea Director for Applebee’s and Brian Proffitt, representative for Apple Colorado LLC. Comments were made by the following member s of the governing body: Dr. Aldrich and Mr. Esquibel. There being no further comments or input and the purpose of the public hearing having been met, Mayor Collins closed the public hearing and referred the application to Finance Committee. ORDINANCE –3rd READING – Creating Section 10.24.200, Vehicle Mufflers, Excessive Smoke and Unreasonable Noise, and repealing Section 8.56.050, Motor Vehicle Mufflers, of the Municipal Code of the City of Cheyenne, Wyoming, to revise and enhance provisions governing vehicle mufflers and noise, to establish a graduated penalty structure for recurring offenses, and to make conforming amendments as specified . Reporting for Public Services Committee, Mr. Segrave moved to approve on third and final reading, seconded by Mr. White. Dr. Aldrich moved to amend Section 10.24.200 to add a subsection H, which includes a review of data after one year, seconded by Mr. Roybal. Motion to amend carried. Voting “yes” – all members of the governing body with the exception of Mr. Laybourn and Mr. Segrave voting “no” . Dr. Aldrich moved to amend Section 10.24.200 subsection H to include a review period of not later than October 31, 2026, seconded by Dr. Rinne. Motion to amend carried. Voting “yes” – all members of the governing body. Main motion as twice amended carried. Voting “yes” – all members of the governing body. items.title: ANNOUNCEMENTS/REPORTS/MOTIONS:
Reappointments of Jennifer Jo Barley-Dunning to the Housing and Community Development Advisory Council, and Aaron Bentley and Dominic Valdez to the Revolving Loan Fund Committee.

Appointments of Ashley Jeffrey and Lexi Leckemby to the Housing and Community Development Advisory Board; Stan Hartzheim to the Downtown Development Authority Board, and Scott VanHorn to the Tourism Promotion Joint Powers Board.
VOUCHER REPORT.
REVENUE REPORT.

Announcement that due to City offices being closed for the Labor Day holiday on Monday, September 1, 2025, regularly scheduled City Council Committee meetings will instead be held in City Council Chambers, 2101 O’Neil Avenue, Cheyenne, Wyoming, and via electronic conference meetings as follows: Public Services Committee will meet Tuesday, September 2, 2025 at Noon and Finance Committee will meet Wednesday, September 3, 2025 at Noon.

Announcement of a Public Hearing to be held September 8, 2025 at 6:00 p.m. in City Council Chambers, 2101 O’Neil Avenue, Cheyenne, WY, and via electronic conference meeting, to determine whether compliance of annexation conditions required by Wyoming Statute §15-1-402 exist for the City-initiated annexation of 35 parcels of land totaling roughly 20.19 acres comprised of various tracts of land and rights-of-way situate in east Cheyenne generally located south of Dell Range Boulevard, west of Dry Creek, east of North College Drive, and north of Cheyenne Street.

Announcement of a Public Hearing to be held September 8, 2025 at 6:00 p.m. in City Council Chambers, 2101 O’Neil Avenue, Cheyenne, WY, and via electronic conference meeting, for a bar & grill liquor license application filed with the City Clerk’s Office for Rich Rich Up LLC d/b/a Wasabi Japanese Steakhouse, 4620 Grandview Ave. #205.

EXECUTIVE SESSION: Pursuant to Wyoming Statute §16-4-405(a)(vii)
ADJOURN.

Motion (per Consent Agenda) carried (accepted bid in an amount not to exceed $662,000.00). (#8240)

Reappointments of Jennifer Jo Barley-Dunning to the Housing and Community Development Advisory Council, and Aaron Bentley and Dominic Valdez to the Revolving Loan Fund Committee. Dr. Aldrich moved to approve, seconded by Mr. Roybal. Motion carried. Voting “yes” – all members of the governing body with the exception of Mayor Collins who did not vote (mayoral appointments).

Appointments of Ashley Jeffrey and Lexi Leck emby to the Housing and Community Development Advisory Board; Stan Hartzheim to the Downtown Development Authority Board, and Scott VanHorn to the Tourism Promotion Joint Powers Board. Dr. Aldrich moved to approve, seconded by Mr. White. Motion carried. Voting “yes” – all members of the governing body with the exception of Mayor Collins who did not vote (mayoral appointments).

of go over the the larger overview um so like I said it's focused on our citywide resources um not so much the department specific websites or social media um and I also want to make sure I acknowledge that all of the the communication efforts and a lot of these projects actually all of these projects are the result of city staff all working together and I've had a lot of help um in all these areas so I wanted to go over some of our existing resources some of our statistics with those um just initiatives that we've had in the last couple years um some potential future projects I'm looking at a few challenges that I just feel are important to point out and then just if you all have any questions so our our bigger um citywide communication tools are obviously our website um it we started with open cities in 2019 and Granicus which is a much larger larger company you might be familiar with purchased Open Cities in 2021 um so we're we're under Granicus now um and of course our items.title: CALL MEETING TO ORDER.
CALL ROLL.
PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE.

CONSENT AGENDA. (All agenda items listed with the designation of are considered to be routine items by the governing body and will be enacted by one motion. There will be no separate discussion on these items unless a member of the governing body so requests and support by two other members is received. Any item removed from the Consent Agenda will be considered in its normal sequence on the agenda.)

Announcement of a Public Hearing to be held July 28, 2025 at 6:00 p.m. in City Council Chambers, 2101 O’Neil Avenue, Cheyenne, WY, and via electronic conference meeting, for a transfer of ownership of restaurant liquor license application filed with the City Clerk’s Office for Pothos Business LLC d/b/a Bella Fuoco, 2115 Warren Ave., Cheyenne, WY (license currently held by Penstemon Business LLC d/b/a Bella Fuoco).

ADJOURN.

Present were: MAYOR – Patrick Collins , COUNCIL MEMBERS – Dr. Michelle Aldrich, Dr. Kathy Emmons, Ken Esquibel, Pete Laybourn, Mark Moody, Dr. Mark Rinne (arrived at 6:13 p.m.), Scott Roybal, Tom Segrave and Jeff White. docs.bodySnippet: 1 RECORD OF PROCEEDINGS FOR THE GOVERNING BODY OF THE CITY OF CHEYENNE Office of City Clerk June 9, 2025 The Governing Body of the City of Cheyenne met in regular session on this date beginning at 6:00 p.m. in Council Chambers and via electronic conference meeting. Present were: MAYOR – Patrick Collins, COUNCIL MEMBERS – Dr. Michelle Aldrich (via Zoom), Dr. Kathy Emmons, Ken Esquibel (via Zoom) , Pete Laybourn, Mark Moody, Dr. Mark Rinne , Scott Roybal, Tom Segrave and Jeff White. Also present: Kylie Soden , City Clerk. The pledge of allegiance was recited. Consent Agenda. (All agenda items listed with the designation of [CA] are considered to be routine items by the governing body and will be enacted by one motion. There will be no separate discussion on these items unless a member of the governing body so requests and support by two other members is received. Any item removed from the Consent Agenda will be considered in its normal sequence on the agenda. Upon request by Mr. Laybourn, and pursuant to support received by Dr. Aldrich and Mr. Moody, item #24(a) was removed from the Consent Agenda. Mr. Segrave moved to approve the remaining items, seconded by Mr. Roybal. Motion carried. Voting “yes” – all members of the governing body. [CA] Minutes from Regular Meeting of the Governing Body on May 2 7, 2025. Motion (per Consent Agenda) carried. Mayor Collins opened a public hearing to determine whether compliance of annexation conditions required by Wyoming Statute §15-1-402 exist for about 199.67 acres of land generally located east of South Greeley Highway and north of Chalk Bluff Road. Public comment was made by: Mark Christensen, AVI PC , agent for the applicant . Comments were made by the following members of the governing body: Dr. Aldrich and Mr. Roybal . There being no further comments or input and the purpose of the public hearing having been met, Mayor Collins closed the public hearing. Mayor Collins opened a public hearing for proposed budgets for the City of Cheyenne and Board of Public Utilities for Fiscal Year 2026. There being no comments or input and the purpose of the public hearing having been met, Mayor Collins closed the public hearing. ORDINANCE –3rd READING – Appropriating moneys for the City of Cheyenne, Wyoming, for the various purposes in conducting the municipal government of said City and fixing the amount of general and special taxes as part of the revenue required to meet the said appropriation, all for the Fiscal Year beginning July 1, 2025, and ending June 30, 2026. Reporting for the Committee of the Whole, Dr. Rinne moved to approve on third and final reading, seconded by Mr. White . Dr. Rinne moved to amend by substitute dated June 5, 2025, seconded by Mr. Roybal. Motion to amend by substitute carried. Voting “yes” – all members of the governing body. Main motion as amended carried. Voting “yes” – all members of the governing body with the exception of Dr. Aldrich, Mr. Laybourn and Mr. Moody voting “no”. Public Services Committee few housekeeping items before we get started please uh mute or turn off your cell phones um during the meeting when making public comment please come to the podium turn on the microphone until it turns green and clearly identify yourself for the record uh to you to make public comment online please use the raise hand function uh let's see there will be no additional Jennifer could we have the first item please number 11 ordinance second reading amending portions of the unified development code modifying provisions related to park impact fees including the timing of fee payment and permitted uses of such fees and making conforming amendments there too mr lloyd please mr chair members of the committee Seth Lloyd with the City of Shine Planning and Development Department um the proposal in front of you is to amend the unified development code to change some aspects regarding park fees these are impact fees that are charged to developments to go toward funding park and recreation facilities um there's two main changes with the park fees uh ordinance in front of you one is to change the timing from the time of platting to the time of permit um we've had some issues with having fees at time of plat um making people not select their zone or fully plat their properties at that time um and then they wait until the last second and then they have a development that's ready and on the get-go and they can't get um they have to go through a platting process which is a council process or a zone change process um and those are long processes they'd have to go through to get ready get their land ready um the second change is um a change to be a little more flexible in the usage of park fees um right now we have three fees which go into two different buckets um the proposal is to change it so we have all three fees going into one bucket for use wherever is needed um this will allow us to get improvements to the population faster so if we need a certain style of improvement to service the new population we can utilize those funds for that type of um service um also with that change we take away the service area concept um Cheyenne isn't the most walkable community and a lot of people drive to various recreation facilities if I have a kid who plays soccer I might not be playing soccer at the park closest to me similar with a playground I may have friends that I want to meet at a playground so I might not be meeting at the closest playground to where I live um so we need recreation facilities located throughout Cheyenne docs.bodySnippet: [Transcript of the meeting video — Work Session - FY 2026 Budget City Clerk & Fire Rescue - 05-08-25] Context/Agenda: # Work Session - FY 2026 Budget City Clerk & Fire Rescue - 05-08-25 Context/Agenda: members online here so we may as well get started Uh madame clerk good afternoon Kylie Soden city clerk today I will presenting I will be presenting the 2026 proposed budget for the city clerk division I'll highlight I'll highlight key light key excuse me key responsibilities summarize the budget explain changes and outline how this budget supports our mission The city clerk's budget starts on page 116 of the budget book The city clerk division plays a critical role in ensuring transparency accountability and efficient city operations The division consists of seven full-time employees and one part-time contract employee We have the city clerk and deputy city clerk positions Wendy Concincaid is our records coordinator Joan Baker is our operations support specialist Tanya Davis and Liz Stoner are business licensing and re receipts clerks Louisa McIll is our operations coordinator and Dennis Dawson provides technical support services involving city-owned property division overview We manage legislative historical and other records including the records retention program oversee business and liquor licensing and permitting maintain city-owned property files and affiliate affiliated database provide municipal clerk election assistance serves as clerk to certain city boards and commissions receipts monies due to the city provides administrative services and maintains records for the cemetery complex Oversee city codebook supplementation oversee and maintain public records request data participate in management of city website and streaming video services for governing body meetings and prepare City Council agendas and minutes Moving into the budget summary 2026 proposed budget $881,98 as compared to 2025's budget of $862,846 The breakdown of those dollars uh payroll accounts for $711,579 contractual services $166,379 and parts and supplies $3,950 Moving into some of the changes I am requesting an additional $1,500 for professional development the increases for certification efforts for the deputy clerk to work towards a certified municipal clerk certification and I would like to continue to pursue municipal master clerk certification Another increase is for software computer software and maintenance I am requesting an additional $12,153 The justification for the computer software increase includes $4,995 to update the Docyphase program This is a onetime fee Docyphase is the city's permanent record software management system The program hasn't been updated in several years and is becoming inefficient I'm also requesting $6,413 to update the Granicus streaming video encoder and software This is also a onetime fee Currently our encoder is out of warranty and needs to be updated from time to time The remaining additional increase accounts for anticipated software annual maintenance increases There are also a few decreases Dues and subscriptions decreased by $380 and printing fees reduced by $200 Both of these decreases reflect closer alignment with actua

docs.bodySnippet: 1 RECORD OF PROCEEDINGS FOR THE GOVERNING BODY OF THE CITY OF CHEYENNE Office of City Clerk April 14, 2025 The Governing Body of the City of Cheyenne met in regular session on this date beginning at 6:00 p.m. in Council Chambers and via electronic conference meeting. Present were: MAYOR – Patrick Collins, COUNCIL MEMBERS – Dr. Michelle Aldrich, Ken Esquibel, Pete Laybourn, Mark Moody, Dr. Mark Rinne , Scott Roybal, Tom Segrave and Jeff White. Absent: Dr. Kathy Emmons. Also present: Kylie Soden, City Clerk. The pledge of allegiance was recited. Consent Agenda. (All agenda items listed with the designation of [CA] are considered to be routine items by the governing body and will be enacted by one motion. There will be no separate discussion on these items unless a member of the governing body so requests and support by two other members is received. Any item removed from the Consent Agenda will be considered in its normal sequence on the agenda. Upon request by Dr. Aldrich, and pursuant to support received by Mr. Moody and Mr. White, item #17(a) was removed from the Consent Agenda. Upon request by Dr. Aldrich, and pursuant to support received by Mr. Esquibel and Mr. Moody, item #19(c) was removed from the Consent Agenda. Dr. Aldrich moved to approve the remaining items, seconded by Mr. Segrave. Motion carried. Voting “yes” – all members of the governing body present. [CA] Minutes from Regular Meeting of the Governing Body on March 24, 2025. Motion (per Consent Agenda) carried. Mayor Collins opened a public hearing for a bar & grill liquor license application filed with the City Clerk’s Office for Frontier Daze, LLC d/b/a Cheba Hut, 3838 Atkin St., Cheyenne, WY. Public comment was made by: Seth Lars en, Cheba Hut. Comments were made by the following members of the governing body: Dr. Aldrich and Mr. Esquibel. There being no further comments or input and the purpose of the hearing having been met, Mayor Collins closed the public hearing and referred the application to Finance Committee. Reporting for Public Services Committee, Mr. Segrave moved to approve on third and final reading, seconded by Mr. White. Motion carried. Voting “yes” – all members of the governing body present. Present were: MAYOR – Patrick Collins , COUNCIL MEMBERS – Dr. Michelle Aldrich, Dr. Kathy Emmons , Ken Esquibel, Pete Laybourn, Mark Moody, Dr. Mark Rinne , Scott Roybal, Tom Segrave and Jeff White. Also present: Kylie Soden, City Clerk. The pledge of allegiance was recited. Consent Agenda. (All agenda items listed with the designation of [CA] are considered to be routine items by the governing body and will be enacted by one motion. There will be no separate discussion on these items unless a member of the governing body so requests and support by two other members is received. Any item removed from the Consent Agenda will be considered in its normal sequence on the agenda . Upon request by Mr. Segrave, and pursuant to support received by Dr. Rinne and Mr. Roybal , item #9 was removed from the Consent Agenda. Upon request by Mr. Moody, and pursuant to support received by Dr. Aldrich and Mr. White, item #12 was removed from the Consent Agenda. Mr. Segrave moved to approve the remaining items, seconded by Dr. Aldrich. Motion carried. Voting “yes” – all members of the governing body. [CA] Minutes from Regular Meeting of the Governing Body on March 10 , 2025. Motion (per Consent Agenda) carried. ORDINANCE –2nd READING – Amending the Official Zoning Map of the City of Cheyenne, changing the zoning classification for land located southwest of the intersection of Wild Bluff and Ogden Road from MR Medium-Density Residential to NR-2 Neighborhood Residential - Medium Density. Reporting for Public Services Committee, Mr. Segrave moved to approve on second reading, seconded by Dr. Emmons . Motion carried. Voting “yes” – all members of the governing body. ORDINANCE –1st READING – Amending Section 10.24.190, Critical Traffic Control Areas; Creation and Administration; Enhanced Penalties, of the Municipal Code of the City of Cheyenne, Wyoming, Modifying the Provisions Governing the Creation and Enforcement of such Areas – referred to Public Services Committee. (Sponsor – Mr. Segrave) ORDINANCE –1st READING – Amending Chapter 10.82, Motor -assisted Scooters, Electric Bicycles, and Bicycles Equipped with GPS of Title 10, Vehicles and Traffic, of the Municipal Code of the City of Cheyenne, Wyoming, authorizing dockless vehicle companies to conduct business in the city using the city's formal procurement process, making a conforming amendment and repealing obsolete provisions – referred to Finance Committee. (Sponsors – Mr. Laybourn and Mr. Segrave) 2 RESOLUTION – Adopting the revised City of Cheyenne, Wyoming, Investment Policy Statement. Reporting for Finance Committee, Mr. Laybourn moved to adopt, seconded by Mr. Esquibel. Dr. Rinne moved to amend Section IV, item number 6 of the policy to add “A minimum of” two non-City employees with financial expertise shall be appointed by the Chairman of the Committee for 2-year terms, seconded by Mr. Segrave. items.title: CALL MEETING TO ORDER.
CALL ROLL.
PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE.

CONSENT AGENDA. (All agenda items listed with the designation of are considered to be routine items by the governing body and will be enacted by one motion. There will be no separate discussion on these items unless a member of the governing body so requests and support by two other members is received. Any item removed from the Consent Agenda will be considered in its normal sequence on the agenda.)
MINUTES FROM REGULAR MEETING OF THE GOVERNING BODY ON FEBRUARY 24, 2025.
MINUTES FROM SPECIAL MEETING OF THE GOVERNING BODY ON FEBRUARY 24, 2025.
PUBLIC HEARINGS:

Public Hearing for a retail liquor license transfer of location application filed with the City Clerk’s Office for F & G Corporation d/b/a The Green Door, from 301 E. Lincolnway to 255 Storey Blvd., Cheyenne, WY.
Public Hearing for the renewal application filed with the City Clerk’s Office for F & G Corporation d/b/a The Green Door, 255 Storey Blvd., Cheyenne, WY.

Public Hearing for a restaurant liquor license application filed with the City Clerk’s Office for Frontier Trampoline Park Inc. d/b/a Frontier Trampoline Park, 3501 E. Lincolnway, Suite B, Cheyenne, WY.
Public Hearing for a restaurant liquor license application filed with the City Clerk’s Office for Thompson-Weaver LLC d/b/a Parkway Pizza, 3753 E. Lincolnway B-6, Cheyenne, WY.

ORDINANCE –3rd READING – Repealing the provisions for the Paid On-Street Parking Districts program of the Municipal Code of the City of Cheyenne, Wyoming, further amending the regulatory authority governing parking in Cheyenne and abrogating any On-Street Parking District designated by Resolution of the Governing Body. (PUBLIC SERVICES COMMITTEE)

ORDINANCE –3rd READING – Amending Sections 1.4.4, 5.1.4 and 5.7.10, of the Unified Development Code to remove the land use term ‘Work Camps’ and prohibit their establishment within the City. (PUBLIC SERVICES COMMITTEE)

ORDINANCE –1st READING – Amending the Official Zoning Map of the City of Cheyenne, changing the zoning classification for land located southwest of the intersection of Wild Bluff and Ogden Road from MR Medium-Density Residential to NR-2 Neighborhood Residential - Medium Density. (SPONSOR – MR. SEGRAVE)
RESOLUTION – Appointing Successor Trustees and designating specified City Officers as Trustees to the City of Cheyenne Health Benefit Trust. (FINANCE COMMITTEE)
RESOLUTION – Certifying the Cheyenne Parks and Recreation Master Plan 2025 for the City of Cheyenne and the Cheyenne Urban Area. (PUBLIC SERVICES COMMITTEE)
RESOLUTION – Adopting the revised City of Cheyenne, Wyoming, Investment Policy Statement. (SPONSORS – DR. RINNE AND MR. SEGRAVE)

RESOLUTION – Granting an exception to the ’201 Agreement’ for the owner of the property located south of High Plains Road and west of South Greeley Highway, between Robert Avenue and Dayshia Lane. (SPONSOR – MR. SEGRAVE)

RESOLUTION – Authorizing the Mayor and the City Clerk to sign a Final Plat for Harmony Valley 5th filing, City of Cheyenne, Laramie County, Wyoming (located between Allison Road and West College Drive, west of Walterscheid Boulevard). (SPONSOR – MR. SEGRAVE)

RESOLUTION – Approving Water and Sanitary Sewer Service by Outside User Agreement for Thunder Basin Land CO LLC, for land located south of High Plains Road and west of South Greeley Highway. (SPONSOR – MR. SEGRAVE)
LEASES/CONTRACTS/LEGAL:

Cooperative Agreement between the City of Cheyenne and the Wyoming Department of Environmental Quality for a FY2024 Clean Water Act, Section 319, Non-Point Source Implementation Grant to assist in construction of the Kiwanis Park Trail and Constructed Wetlands Project. (FY2024 CWA Section 319 Grant) (FINANCE COMMITTEE)

Professional Services Agreement between the City of Cheyenne and Great Western Installations, Inc., for the Optimist Park – Playground Design and Installation. (CDBG-Parks Projects Grant and Development Impact Fees) (FINANCE COMMITTEE)
items.action: Approve in an amount not to exceed $299,825.46

items.title: Agreement between the Cheyenne Civic Center and Local 229 of the International Alliance of Theatrical Stage Employees, Moving Picture Technicians, Artists and Allied Crafts of the United States, for production services. (Civic Center Fund)
2025-2026 Collective Labor Agreement between the City of Cheyenne and Cheyenne Firefighters, Local Union No. 279, International Association of Firefighters.
Professional Services Agreement between the City of Cheyenne and Trihydro Corporation for the Landfill Compliance Monitoring Services. (Solid Waste Fund)
CONTRACT MODIFICATIONS:

Contract Modification #1 to Contract #7520 between the City of Cheyenne and Benchmark Engineers, PC for additional engineering services for the Christensen Road Design Modifications project. (2017 Specific Purpose Option Tax Fund)

Contract Modification #2 to Contract #7866 between the City of Cheyenne, Office of Youth Alternatives and Laramie County School District #1 to extend the contract for community and crisis counseling services. (Revenue to City)
CONSIDERATION OF BIDS/PURCHASES/REQUESTS FOR PROPOSALS:
Consideration of Bid #E-12-25 for As-Needed Emergency Snow Control for the Public Works Department. (2023-2026 Optional 1% Sales Tax Fund) (FINANCE COMMITTEE)
items.action: Accept bid from S&S Builders, Full Tilt, and Knife River in an    amount not to exceed $300,000.00 for a period of 3 years

items.title: Consideration of Bid #S-15-25 for an Agreement between the City of Cheyenne and Quality Electric for the Cheyenne Fire Rescue – Installation of Owner Provided Backup Generators for Stations #2 and #6 project. (Development Impact Fees and Homeland Security Grant)
APPLICATIONS/LICENSES/PERMITS:

Renewal applications for existing City liquor licenses (retail, restaurant, limited retail, resort, bar and grill licenses, microbrewery, satellite distillery, special malt beverage and winery permits) filed with the City Clerk’s Office. (FINANCE COMMITTEE)
ANNOUNCEMENTS/REPORTS/MOTIONS:
VOUCHER REPORT.
OTHER BUSINESS:
ADJOURN.

docs.bodySnippet: RECORD OF PROCEEDINGS FOR THE GOVERNING BODY OF THE CITY OF CHEYENNE Office of City Clerk February 24, 2025 The Governing Body of the City of Cheyenne met in special session on this date beginning at 7:35 p.m. in Council Chambers and via electronic conference meeting, for the purpose of collective labor bargaining with the Cheyenne Professional Firefighters, International Association of Firefighters, Local No. 279. Present were: MAYOR – Patrick Collins, COUNCIL MEMBERS – Dr. Michelle Aldrich, Dr. Kathy Emmons, Ken Esquibel, Pete Laybourn, Mark Moody, Scott Roybal, Tom Segrave and Jeff White. Absent: Dr. Mark Rinne. Also present: Kylie Soden, City Clerk, Amber Ash, Chief of Staff, John Brodie, City Attorney, Robin Lockman, City Treasurer and Chief John Kopper and Deputy Chief Andrew Dykshorn, Cheyenne Fire Rescue. The pledge of allegiance was recited. Mayor Collins provided opening comments and noted the importance of the labor management discussions that occur leading up to negotiations. He provided meeting room location information that would be used for the purpose of caucusing if needed. The proposed Ground Rules were agreed upon and signed by the City and Union. [Clerk’s note: City’s Spokespersons we re Mayor Patrick Collins, City Attorney John Brodie and City Council Vice President Scott Roybal. The Union’s Spokespersons were Neil Durante, Vincent McQueeney and Chris Thoms .] Mayor Collins and Vincent McQueeney, Spokesperson for the Cheyenne Professional Firefighters, International Association of Firefighters, Local No. 279, expressed mutual appreciation for their continued collaboration in working together on the Collective Labor Agreement. Mayor Collins and Union Spokesperson McQueeney reviewed the proposed agreement which included changes to the following: Section 2 – Definitions; Section 4 – Term of Agreement; Section 13 – Management Rights; Section 15 – Department Staffing; Section 21 – Classification of Employment and Basic Wages; Section 22 – Overtime; Section 23 – Working in a Highter Job Rank; Section 24 – Conversion of Benefit Hours; Section 25 – Wellness/Fitness Program; Section 27 – Sick Leave and Section 42 – Longevity Pay. Mayor Collins and Mr. McQueeney announced acceptance of the proposed agreement as written. There bein g no fur ther business to come before the governing body, the meeting was officially adjourned at 8:04 p.m. Submitted by, Kylie Soden, Deputy City Clerk This notice is available in alternative, accessible formats upon request. Published: Wyoming Tribune-Eagle March 5, 2025

VOUCHER REPORT.

ADJOURN.

docs.bodySnippet: [Transcript of the meeting video — Finance Committee 02-04-25 1] Context/Agenda: # Finance Committee 02-04-25 Context/Agenda: good afternoon welcome to the February 4th 2025 Finance Committee meeting I'd like to ask the public and the staff to turn off cell phones or put them to vibrate or mute so that we can uh not be disturbed when making public comment clearly identify yourself to make public comment online use the raised hand function online in person approach the podium and please turn on the microphone there will be no additional business that will be be discussed at the completion of the agenda clerk please read the first item number 11b lease agreement between the city of Cheyenne and the Girl Scouts of Montana and Wyoming for 45.93 Acres of city-owned real property located near the former Roundtop water treatment facility to be used for the purposes of conducting activities consistent with the bylaws and Articles of Incorporation of the Girl Scouts of Montana and Wyoming Revenue to the city is there a staff report Mr chair Jason Sanchez Community reckon events uh this is a partnership we've had with the Girl Scouts uh for many decades um it's we put a one-year contract on this one just because we we're waiting to see what the action is from the at the legislature in regard to our partnership with our potential partnership with the state um the girl scats Montana have used the cam Carefree area for again many many uh decades uh they take good care of it and in Lou they pay $100 a year for use and help with maintenance and I'll stand by for questions and I believe we have a representative from the Girl Scouts of Montana online Mr Ro Mr rorn do do the Girl Scouts still utilize it as much as they used to Mr chair through you that is correct they use almost all 49 Acres okay thank you thank you Mr chair yes um do you probably more for the representative for the Girl Scouts but what do we receive from Montana in not an exchange wouldn't be the word but do the Girl Scouts of Wyoming have a place up in Montana that is similar to this that they're able to use yes we we have uh can you hear me yeah we can hear
